about: What's new, shown once after an update (tutorial.js). Newest first. v = the version number the change went live in; lines = one or two short sentences a player understands. MAIN adds an entry at each merge: v is the version on the default branch before the merge, plus 1.

lines: Taught: Korvold, Fae-Cursed King. When it enters or attacks you sacrifice another permanent, and every sacrifice gives it a +1/+1 counter and draws you a card.
Every kind of sacrifice now counts for "whenever you sacrifice" cards: costs, fetch lands, edicts, upkeep costs, Sagas and the rest (also Juri, Havoc Jester, Blood Aspirant).
What's new now shows one card per update. Swipe, or use Back and Next, to read older ones.
Cards the simulator doesn't fully understand yet have one button: Request Cards to be added. It sends only the card names, never your list.
Triggered and activated abilities now choose their targets when they go on the stack, as the rules require. If a response removes the target, the ability does nothing to it; it never picks a new one.

Combo wins are now checked for legality: each combo pays its startup cost (Basalt Monolith + Rings needs its first 5 mana), Underworld Breach needs real fuel and a finisher you can cast, and the game log lists every combo step.
Mox Amber makes only the colours of your legendary creatures and planeswalkers, Reflecting Pool only what your other lands make, and Arcane Signet and Command Tower only your commander's colours.

Tap any card in Practice, Duel or Pod, including the cards on a question sheet, to open it large with its actions as buttons: Cast, Play land, abilities, loyalty, attack or block, pick a target. Swipe to the next card in the same row.

Planeswalker ultimates taught: Ral Crackling Wit, both Tamiyos, Wrenn and Seven, Tezzeret Master of the Bridge, Ral Zarek, Saheeli the Gifted, plus Teferi Who Slows the Sunset, Ral Storm Conduit and Estrid's +2. More "Activate only if…" limits are enforced (Sea Gate Wreckage, Resonating Lute, Endless Atlas, Luminarch Ascension…).

Taught in full: Nahiri the Harbinger, Nahiri the Lithomancer, Ob Nixilis of the Black Oath (+2), Lord Windgrace, Minsc & Boo (−2), Sorin Imperious Bloodlord (+1), Tevesh Szat (+1), Tezzeret Cruel Captain (0), Tyvar Kell (+1), Kaito Cunning Infiltrator (+1) and Professor Onyx.
Chandra, Awakened Inferno's −X can now hit a planeswalker as well as a creature.
Planeswalker abilities with −X that deal damage now really remove X loyalty. You pick X; the autopilot pays the smallest X that does the job.

Taught in full: Chandra, Awakened Inferno; Chandra, Flamecaller; Commodore Guff; Dihada; Domri; Jace, Mirror Mage; Kaito, Bane of Nightmares; Narset of the Ancient Way; and Jaya Ballard's +1. Mana that can only be spent on certain spells is now tracked.

Honest card reading: a planeswalker or activated ability now counts as understood only when ICEYfish plays every sentence of it. Cards that dropped part of their text now show as not fully understood, so you can teach them.

Taught in full: Nicol Bolas, Dragon-God; both Ugins; Elspeth, Storm Slayer; Nissa, Who Shakes the World; Grist; Thrasios; Raging Ravine; Liliana, Death's Majesty; and 20 more cards from the built-in decks. "Activate only if…" limits (Minas Tirith, Idol of Oblivion…) are now enforced.

Swipe through cards: with a card open large, swipe left or right (or use the arrow keys) to move to the card next to it in the same row. It stops at the ends and shows "3 of 7". Puzzle first; the other tables follow.

Top of your library: with Bolas's Citadel, Mystic Forge, Future Sight, Courser of Kruphix or Experimental Frenzy in play, tap the face-up top card to play it: Play land, Cast, or Cast for N life (Citadel, plus any tax like Thalia's). What isn't allowed shows greyed with the reason.
X can now be 0 when you cast an X spell.
Tidal Loop (Hakbal): its Drive name now says Bracket 5; ICEYfish's check keeps it at Bracket 4 (Bracket 5 needs a win before turn 4 on average; its median is turn 7).
Taught: Ajani, Sleeper Agent. His +1 reveals the top card (creature or planeswalker to hand, otherwise you may bottom it), −3 lets you split three +1/+1 counters, and Compleated loyalty is right.

Taught: Chandra, Torch of Defiance. Her first +1 exiles the top card and lets you cast it, or deals 2 damage to each opponent if you don't; her −7 makes the emblem that deals 5 damage whenever you cast a spell.
On a phone, Practice, Duel and Pod now show the tabs in two rows of four, like every other screen.
New built-in deck: Blood Bank (Edgar Markov). Its Drive name says Bracket 4; ICEYfish's check puts it at Bracket 3 (3 Game Changers, no cheap combo, turn-7 median kill).
Taught: Master of Dark Rites. Tap it and sacrifice another creature for {B}{B}{B}, which only pays for Vampire, Cleric or Demon spells.
Full priority is on: spells, triggers and abilities now go on a real stack, the way the Comprehensive Rules have it, so you and the autopilot can respond to each one in turn.
Cast triggers now resolve before the spell that caused them, so a few game results shift slightly.
Rules Lawyers (Winota) is updated to its newest list from Drive (14 cards changed, still Bracket 4).
Taught: Sorin, Vengeful Bloodlord. Your creatures and planeswalkers have lifelink during your turn, and his −X returns a creature card with mana value X from your graveyard as a Vampire.
Duel on an upright phone: the whole top bar fits on the screen again, with no sideways scrolling to reach the playmat, sound and help buttons.

New, off by default: Settings → Display → Guess unknown rules. A rules line ICEYfish can't read yet is played like the closest line it knows, marked "guessed N%" with the card it was matched to. Guesses can be wrong, so the card stays on the Teach list.
Puzzles: tap a card to open it large, with its actions (Cast, Play, abilities, Attack) as buttons inside, next to its prices and printings.
New built-in deck: Rules Lawyers (Winota, Joiner of Forces), checked as Bracket 4.
ICEYfish now carries its copyright notice (SWD Marketing, all rights reserved), and the app's own tests run more reliably.

More groundwork for full priority: activated abilities now pay their cost and wait on the stack, so there is a chance to respond, and the autopilot can respond during blocks and damage. Still switched off, so games play as before.
More groundwork for full priority: triggered abilities now wait on the stack with a chance to respond between each one. Still switched off, so games play as before.
Groundwork for full priority and a real stack (the Comprehensive Rules' way of responding to spells and triggers). It stays switched off for now, so games play as before.
Proliferate lets you choose: pick which permanents and players get one more of each counter they have.

Timing follows the rules more closely: extra turns are no longer capped, beginning-of-combat triggers fire in every combat, deaths and lifelink resolve between first-strike and regular damage, and "next end step" effects wait for the next end step.
The speed bar and table controls should look sharp on iPhone and iPad.
Puzzles: you choose how each cost is paid (Rocks before the dragon can be won by hand now), and the Puzzle tab fits phones: two rows of tabs up to 430 px wide.
Duel on phones: a 🔁 Loop button on the game bar. Simulate's sample games replay on the real Practice table, where you can take over at any turn.
Entrancing Melody: choose X, then a creature with mana value X to take.
Taught on request: Cemetery Gatekeeper, Cori Mountain Monastery, Shadow Alley Denizen and Vampire Nocturnus. Intimidate now limits blockers as it should.
Groundwork for sending card corrections without signing in to anything: once it's switched on, "Teach these cards" and deck saves go straight to ICEYfish.
Mana Tithe now gets cast against you and asks if you'll pay {1}. Demonic Consultation lets you name the card, even one that isn't in your library.
Basalt and Grim Monolith loops can be played by hand: untap from the card menu, then pick how much mana to make. Port Razer gets its extra combat.
Puzzles: the Medium and Hard fast wins now end four different ways (Thassa's Oracle, Jace, Laboratory Maniac, a Vito drain), and you cast every piece yourself; the order matters.
New deck: Winota (Winota, Joiner of Forces), Bracket 4.
More cards read exactly: Aether Vial, Breath of Fury, Clarion Conqueror, Spirit of the Labyrinth, Greymond, Slicer, Zurzoth, High Noon and others. Signal Pest's battle cry works now.
The Puzzle tab is back with 12 new puzzles: win by turn 2–3 from your opening hand, or find the one line that finishes a late game. Easy, Medium and Hard; the opponent's hand stays hidden.
A wrong play plays out; afterwards you get hints (never the answer), and every puzzle ends with the mechanic it teaches.

More cards answer spells as they're cast: Return the Favor, Wandering Archaic, Ricochet Trap, Hydroelectric Specimen, Disrupting Shoal, Orim's Chant, Autumn's Veil, Royal Treatment and Legolas's Quick Reflexes. Boromir counters spells cast without mana.
Redirect Lightning can now redirect bounce and burn spells too.
Two new Avatar decks: Heavy Metal Landfall (Toph, the First Metalbender, Bracket 3) and Landslide Victory (Bumi, Unleashed, Bracket 4).
Decks are listed by their official bracket (or by color); win rates and kill turns are gone from the deck menus for now.

Cards can now answer a spell as it's cast: Redirect Lightning and Hullbreaker Horror. Also read exactly: Selvala, Hanweir Battlements, Sword of the Paruns, Teysa, Firestorm, Avarice Totem and 11 more.
The Puzzle tab is hidden while the puzzles are rebuilt.
On phones and iPads a tap selects a card first (lifted and enlarged with its options); nothing is played until you tap an option. Undo can't take back a play that revealed new cards.
Change a card's printing from the card viewer anywhere (Build, Practice, Duel, Pod): one tap switches it everywhere the deck shows it.
"Save to my Drive" puts a pasted deck straight into your Drive folder for teaching. New: the Puzzle tab (win by turn 2, Easy to Hard, with score and streaks) and a "The fastest deck" tutorial.
Floating mana now empties at the end of each step and phase, and more cards are read exactly (Clock of Omens, Liquimetal, Cursed Mirror and others).

More cards read exactly: Noxious Gearhulk gains life equal to the destroyed creature's toughness, Heliod's Intervention destroys X targets, Demon of Fate's Design casts enchantments for life, Ramos makes mana, River Kelpie and Neyali (graveyards and attacking tokens).
You choose which lands and sources pay (on by default, in Settings), with no wasted mana and a warning before floating mana is lost. Rhystic Study and Smothering Tithe taxes use the same sheet.
The top bar is sharp, the step strip stays still on every phone, and Practice shows the steps too. The default table felt has no glow.
Firebending, Waterbend and Airbend work as written.
Signets make mana now (pay {1}, get two colours). They were doing nothing before, so the 11 decks that play them get faster.
A deck you paste that has cards ICEYfish doesn't fully read gets a "Save to Drive for teaching" button: save it in your ManaBox folder and its cards are taught within the hour.
Earthbend works as written: any land you control (stack counters on one already earthbent), chosen as it's cast, and it comes back tapped once. Toph, the First Metalbender turns artifacts into lands.
Twinflame copies as many of your creatures as you pay Strive for. Teferi, Temporal Archmage's −1 untaps four permanents.
Settings: the Spacing choice is gone; everyone gets Standard.
Springleaf Drum works: tap it and an untapped creature (even one that just arrived) for one mana of any colour. Survivors' Encampment and similar lands now need that creature too.
Every card in the built-in decks is now fully understood: Gisa and Kaervek's crimes count when a spell is cast, Gideon's +1 makes a real 5/5, plus Chrome Dome, Okina and Multiversal Passage.
Computer players pay a Rhystic Study or Smothering Tithe tax only with mana they don't need this turn.
Phyrexian mana costs what the card says: the colour or 2 life (Dismember, Gitaxian Probe, Mental Misstep…). Before, it was free. When you can do either, you choose.
While you choose attackers: "Attacking for N" counts your damage as you go (double strike, poison, commander damage, LETHAL). Defending shows what's incoming and what gets through.
A poison counter (☠ N/10) sits next to each player's commander damage, red from 8.
Settings has "Choose how I pay mana": pick which lands and sources pay, and which colour each makes. Off by default.
Sylvan Library plays out in full: draw two more, then pay 4 life or put back each of two cards. Imprint cards (Chrome Mox, Isochron Scepter…) let you choose the card.
Play a friend reconnects by itself after a phone sleeps or the network drops, codes games included.
Duel, Pod and Play a friend: a turn timer (90 seconds for your first 5 turns, 60 after). Run out and your turn ends, womp womp. Switch it off in Settings.
Fierce Guardianship and friends can always answer a spell (free with your commander out). Rhystic Study, Smothering Tithe and similar cards ask the player to pay or not.
Five more of your Drive decks are in the deck chooser, bracket-checked. Settings has a Deck order: bracket then rank (the default), color then bracket, or color then rank.
Duel and Pod: the roll-for-first dice now show on every screen (they could be heard but not seen on some phones).
Proliferate (Atraxa, Praetors' Voice and friends) lets you pick from every permanent with a counter, an opponent's too, and the log says what it added.
Mystic Forge, Bolas's Citadel, Future Sight and similar cards show your top card face up (only to you). Courser of Kruphix and friends show it to everyone.
Explore shows the revealed card to every player. Urza's Saga's chapter III lets you choose the artifact, and Sagas now count up after your draw.

Against an opponent, a spell's target is chosen when it is cast, as the rules say. Before you decide whether to counter, you see what it targets ("Targeting your Serra Angel" or "Targeting you"). If the target is gone when it resolves, the spell does nothing to it.
Bill the Pony, Meriadoc Brandybuck and Spike Feeder play as written.
When a game ends: Play again, Change deck or Leave. In Play a friend your friend gets a rematch request, and Leave tells them you left.
Play a friend has no autopilot: each player makes every choice themselves.
Tags starts fully folded, groups too: tap its header to open it.
Odds: the Draw odds graph shows straight away (your ramp, else card draw, else lands). Pick other cards under Choose cards.

More cards play as written: life lost this turn (Essence Channeler, Luminarch Ascension), manifest (Ugin's Mastery), Fiend Artisan, dice rolls (Wyll, Component Pouch, Treasure Chest), copy spells (Fire Lord Azula, Double Major) and finality counters (Meathook Massacre II).
Isochron Scepter: the Vitalize combo with creatures that untap the Scepter now works, and split cards like Fire // Ice can't go under it (their mana value is the total).

Transmute fetches the missing combo piece, can find lands (Tolaria West), only works when you could cast a sorcery, and is used instead of casting the card when that gets to a combo sooner. All 14 transmute cards are in.
Table fixes: 540-px-high sideways screens get the side-by-side table, Confirm blocks stays in view on short screens, and crowded Pod opponents no longer run off the edge.
29 more popular cards play as written, among them Zimone, Underrealm Lich, Wall of Roots, Aetherworks Marvel and Sidisi. Mill triggers and rad counters now work too.
Tables fit every iPhone and iPad, upright and sideways, and 1920×1080 screens. On a dual-screen device, each side of the table gets its own screen, with nothing under the hinge.
Pages are much more compact: report boxes fold to their headers (tap a header to open it).
Practice and Duel/Pod tables fill the whole screen. ☰ brings the menu back, and ⛶ goes full screen where your browser allows it.
A second run starts faster: the app keeps its game workers warm between runs.
The A/B deck test and its card check run on every core too, and a run that loses a helper carries on instead of stopping.
Tune, Tune to the next bracket and the Policy lab use every core of your device: about twice as fast, with the same answers.
Play a friend: on the same Wi-Fi your friend shows up under Nearby. Tap their name, they accept, and you play: no codes. On different networks, both type the same room name.
A dropped connection now comes back by itself, and the screen stays awake during a game.
Raise your combo odds: "Try your own" refuses a card outside your commander's colours, and Apply leaves your Sideboard alone and survives a reload.
Simulate, Mirror match and Pod runs use every core of your device, so they finish much faster, with the same results as before.
Eight more cards play as written: Brutalizer Exarch, Great Oak Guardian, Llanowar Loamspeaker, Marvin, Prime Speaker Vannifar, Riptide Shapeshifter, The Notary Hobbits and Michelangelo, the Heart.
Play a friend connects directly (WebRTC) only: no relay server any more. If a direct connection can't be made, it says so and suggests the same Wi-Fi or another network.
Two new built-in decks: Short Circuit (Vivi Ornitier), checked at Bracket 4, and Dead Ringers (Ratadrabik of Urborg), checked at Bracket 3.

Ten more cards understood, including Solemnity (its persist and undying loops now play out as a combo), Mikaeus, the Unhallowed, Fiend Hunter and Marionette Apprentice. Fixed rare endless-loop crashes.

Combos: the autopilot keeps and assembles your combos and plays them out to the win. In Practice you're told when one is assembled and asked what to do: go off, how much mana (∞ for infinite), mill, draw your deck, or wait.
Infinite mana shows as ∞ in the mana pool.
Cauldron of Souls gives your creatures persist when they're at risk, and Aerie Ouphes (new) can shoot down an opponent's flyer and come back with persist.
Raise your combo odds suggests only cards in your commander's colours (and legal in Commander), shows a progress bar, and has a ✕ on each suggestion that brings in the next best piece.

Simulate: Tune to the next bracket finds card swaps and play changes that make your deck kill faster, checks them over 2,000 games, and tells you what to change. Apply one or all; nothing changes until you do.
New built-in deck: Overtime at the Treasure Mine (Magda, Brazen Outlaw), checked at Bracket 4.
More cards understood, including Master Biomancer, Saruman, the White Hand, Geode Golem (it still pays the commander tax) and Joraga Treespeaker.
Mobile Garrison untaps another artifact or creature when it attacks, and Fire-Belly Changeling's pump stops after two a turn.
Odds: a Combo odds box shows your chance of having every piece of a combo by each turn. Simulate: Raise your combo odds suggests one-card additions and lets you try your own swap.
A deck the Commander rule refuses no longer leaves the deck menu on the wrong deck.
Fixed rare game errors (a creature with echo that lost its abilities; a blanked mana rock). Blockers' damage is doubled by Uncivil Unrest, Neriv and the like too.
Policy lab: a short run says it needs more turns instead of guessing a bracket.
Rune of Flight on an Equipment gives the equipped creature flying. Every card from your Teach requests is now fully understood.
27 more cards play by their rules, among them Shalai and Hallar, Neriv, The Ooze and Galadriel. The Sound of Drums and Inquisitor's Flail double combat damage only.
A Commander deck must be 100 cards: a commander and 99, or two commanders and 98. Build says what is off; a bigger deck loads when its list has a // Specialty line.
Every built-in deck's bracket was checked over 20,000 games and the official bracket rules. Mermaids, The King's Gambit and Tidecaller are bracket 4.
⚔️ A little battle plays under the progress bar while games run (switch it off in the Sound panel 🔊).
Magda, Return the Favor, Axgard Cavalry, Vault Robber, Óin the Brave and Dwarven Bloodboiler now play by their rules; in Duel and Pod you're asked before each one acts.
Play a friend: the connection bar no longer stays on "Not connected" after a quiet moment.
Duel and Pod ask how many times to pay squad, and which mode of a Will card to choose (one or both with your commander out).
Play a friend on phones and tablets: a game no longer sometimes fails to start, and taps on the table are no longer lost.
Took's Adventure is no longer a built-in deck. A game with Luminous Broodmoth and Elesh Norn no longer stops with an error.
More than 30 more cards now play by their rules, among them Sliver Legion, March of the World Ooze, Kykar and Elenda. Squad and the Will cards' modes work too.
When a card pumps an attacker of your choice, Duel and Pod ask you which one.
The Practice sample game says when the autopilot plays on to a turn, and lets you go on while it plays.
On a PC the app now uses the whole screen: Practice fits one 1920×1080 screen, and Simulate shows three charts a row.
Build → More rules: mulligan down to, your starting life, no maximum hand size, and Reset. Display: spacing and tab-switch speed.
Simulate → Policy lab → Tune toward a goal: make the deck kill earlier or hit its land drops more often, and see the bracket speed it reaches.
The Duel tours now show Play a friend, with a one-time tip if you have seen them before.
🎲 Turn the dice and coin animations on or off in the Sound panel (🔊).
With your commander out, choose one mode or both on Jeska's Will and Akroma's Will, and pick the creature Hostage Taker or Gilded Drake takes.
Simulations start at 2,000 games, so results come back faster. Type a bigger number for more precision.
Every feature: a long tour of each tab, or of every tab, under ?.
Play a friend is back: duel someone on another device from the Duel tab.
New to ICEYfish? Tap ? for a sample game, your first goals and this list.
Shock lands ask whether to pay 2 life, and more cards ask you before they decide.
Tours: each tab explains itself the first time you open it. Tap ? to see a tour again.
ICEYfish remembers where you were: your tab, deck, settings and Practice game survive a reload.
Duel and Pod: everyone rolls a d20 to see who goes first.
Melded cards come together with an animation.
3D dice and coins.
